p5.q: When Mr. Adeyemi retires in June, he ______ at the Lagos assembly plant for exactly twenty-two years.
p5.exp: 「六月退休時」是未來的時間點，到那時「已經做滿 22 年」，要用未來完成式 will have worked。when 子句用現在式 retires 表示未來，是時間子句的規則。has worked 是現在完成式，只算到現在為止；had worked 是過去完成式，用在過去某時點之前；is working 是現在進行式，不能搭配 for exactly twenty-two years 這種「到某時點為止的累計期間」。

p5.q: The loading dock on the east side of the warehouse ______ this week, so all deliveries should use the north gate.
p5.exp: 碼頭是「被」重新鋪路面，要用被動；this week 表示工程正在進行中，所以用現在進行式的被動 is being resurfaced。is resurfacing、has resurfaced、resurfaces 都是主動語態，等於說碼頭自己去鋪路面，不合邏輯。

p5.q: When the auditors requested the files, most of the paper receipts ______ to the archive in Rotterdam.
p5.exp: 收據是「被」轉移，要被動；而且轉移發生在查帳人員索取檔案（過去）之前，要用過去完成式被動 had already been transferred。have already been transferred 是現在完成式，和過去的 requested 時間對不上；were already transferring 和 had already transferred 都是主動，等於收據自己去搬別的東西。

p5.q: Since the two hotel chains merged, the number of loyalty program members ______ to more than four million.
p5.exp: Since + 過去時間點（合併之後）一路到現在，主要子句用現在完成式。主詞是 the number（數目），是單數，所以用 has grown。grew 是單純過去式，不能和 since 連用；is growing 是進行式，不表示「從那時到現在累積」；had grown 是過去完成式，需要另一個過去時間點當基準。

p5.q: The new prices will appear on the company website only after the regional managers ______ the final figures.
p5.exp: after 引導的時間子句即使講的是未來，也不能用 will，要用現在式或現在完成式；強調「核准完成之後」才上架，用 have approved。will approve 違反時間子句的規則；would approve 是條件或過去的未來；had approved 是過去完成式，和主要子句的 will appear（未來）時間對不上。

p5.q: At this time next Monday, the logistics team ______ the first shipment from the new Busan facility.
p5.exp: At this time next Monday（下週一的這個時候）指未來某個時刻「正在進行」的動作，要用未來進行式 will be unloading。has unloaded 是現在完成式；unloads 是現在簡單式，不表示某一刻正在做；had been unloading 是過去完成進行式，用於過去。

p5.q: The quality inspector ______ the second batch of valves when she noticed a hairline crack in one of the casings.
p5.exp: 「正在檢查時，突然發現裂縫」：進行中的背景動作用過去進行式 was examining，被打斷的短暫動作用過去式 noticed。has examined、examines、will examine 的時間都和過去式 noticed 對不上。

p5.q: Ms. Ferreira ______ the hotel's banquet department since it reopened in 2023, and guest ratings have risen every year.
p5.exp: since it reopened in 2023 表示從過去持續到現在，要用現在完成（進行）式 has been managing，強調一直在管理。managed 是過去式，不能接 since 子句；is managing 是現在進行式，無法表達「從 2023 年到現在」；will manage 是未來式。

p5.q: All forklift operators ______ by a certified instructor before they are allowed to work on the warehouse floor.
p5.exp: 後面有 by a certified instructor（由合格講師），可見操作員是「被訓練」的一方，助動詞後接被動 be trained：must be trained。must train 是主動，變成操作員去訓練別人；must have trained 是「當時一定已經訓練過」的推測，而且也是主動；must 後面不能接 V-ing，所以 must training 文法錯誤。

p5.q: Several of the company's older delivery vans ______ with electric models, cutting the fleet's fuel costs considerably.
p5.exp: 舊貨車是「被」電動車取代，replace A with B 的被動是 A be replaced with B，加上 recently（最近）搭配現在完成式：have recently been replaced。have recently replaced 是主動，變成貨車去取代別的東西；recently 不和進行式或未來式搭配，所以 are recently replacing、will recently replace 都不對。

p5.q: The marketing department ______ its brand guidelines nearly two years ago and plans to update them again this winter.
p5.exp: nearly two years ago（將近兩年前）是明確的過去時間，只能用過去式 revised。現在完成式 has revised 不能和 ago 連用；had revised 需要另一個更晚的過去時點當基準；will revise 和 ago 矛盾。

p5.q: Before the resort reopens in April, all 240 guest rooms ______ with new carpets, furniture, and lighting.
p5.exp: 四月重新開幕前（未來時點）「客房已經被翻新完成」，要用未來完成式的被動 will have been refurbished。will have refurbished 是主動，房間不會自己翻新；had been refurbished 是過去完成式，和未來的 reopens 不搭；are refurbishing 也是主動語態。

p5.q: Last quarter's revenue figures ______ until the external auditors had verified every major transaction.
p5.exp: 營收數字是「被發布」，要被動；Last quarter（上一季）和 had verified 都指過去，所以用過去式被動 were not released。did not release 是主動，數字不會自己發布；have not been released 是現在完成式，和 until 子句中的過去完成式 had verified 對不上；are not released 是現在式。

p5.q: Ms. Lindqvist ______ the supplier's billing office three times before anyone finally returned her call yesterday.
p5.exp: 回電發生在 yesterday（過去），而聯絡三次又發生在回電「之前」，比過去更早的動作用過去完成式 had contacted。has contacted 是現在完成式，不能搭配以 yesterday 為基準的敘述；contacts、will contact 時間都不對。

p5.q: The ______ a shipment is booked, the lower the freight rate the carrier is usually willing to offer.
p5.exp: 「the + 比較級……, the + 比較級……」表示「越……就越……」。後半句是 the lower，前半句也要用比較級 the earlier（越早訂）。earliest 是最高級；early 是原級；early 的比較級是 earlier，不說 more early。

p5.q: The new packaging line is not nearly as ______ as the equipment supplier's brochure had suggested.
p5.exp: as ... as 中間放原級：not nearly as reliable as（遠不如……可靠）。as more reliable as、as most reliable as 都是錯誤組合；be 動詞 is 後面要形容詞，副詞 reliably 不行。

p5.q: Of the three venues the event planners visited, the riverside hotel was clearly the ______ suitable for a large banquet.
p5.exp: Of the three（三者之中）比較三個以上的對象，用「the + 最高級」：the most suitable。more 是比較級，用於兩者比較；much、many 不能放在 the 和形容詞 suitable 之間表示比較。

p5.q: Ms. Novak's proposal was ______ costly than the other bids, yet it also included two years of free maintenance.
p5.exp: 後面有 than，要用比較級；less costly than 表示「比……便宜」，和 yet（卻還）附帶免費維修的語意也相符。least 是最高級，不接 than；fewer 修飾可數名詞的數量，不能修飾形容詞 costly；little 是原級。

p5.q: This quarter, the call center received ______ complaints than in any other quarter since it opened in 2021.
p5.exp: complaints 是可數名詞複數，「比較少」用 fewer，加上 than 是比較級：fewer complaints than。less 用於不可數名詞，是常見錯誤；fewest、least 是最高級，不能接 than。

p5.q: The upgraded sorting system can process ______ 9,000 parcels per hour, three times its previous capacity.
p5.exp: as many as + 數字 + 可數名詞，表示「多達……」，parcels（包裹）可數，用 as many as。as much as 用於不可數名詞或金額；as more as 不合文法，as ... as 中間要原級；so much as 多用於否定句（not so much as），在此意思不通。

p5.q: Sales of the compact model were strong last year, but this year's figures are ______ more impressive.
p5.exp: 加強比較級 more impressive 要用 even、much、far、still 等字：even more impressive（甚至更驚人）。very 只能修飾原級，不能說 very more；so、too 也不能直接修飾比較級。

p5.q: The new staff uniforms are made from the ______ fabric as the old ones but have a more modern cut.
p5.exp: 後面接 as the old ones，固定說法是 the same + 名詞 + as（和……一樣的）。similar 要搭配 to（similar to）；identical 也要搭配 to；alike 只能放在 be 動詞後當補語，不能直接修飾名詞 fabric。

p5.q: In independent tests, the premium blender proved ______ to competing models in both durability and noise level.
p5.exp: superior to（優於）是拉丁字源的比較字，後面接 to 而不是 than。better、higher、greater 都是一般比較級，後面要接 than，不能接 to。

p5.q: The company's new warehouse in Leeds is nearly three times ______ the facility it replaced.
p5.exp: 倍數比較可以用「倍數 + the size of + 名詞」：three times the size of（是……的三倍大）。as size as 錯在 as ... as 中間要放形容詞（應為 as large as）；larger as 錯在 larger 要接 than 不接 as；bigger to 錯在 bigger 要接 than 不接 to。

p5.q: The quoted repair cost was no ______ than the amount already set aside in the maintenance budget.
p5.exp: no + 比較級 + than 表示「不超過、不比……高」：no higher than。high 是原級，不能接 than；highest 是最高級；high 的比較級是 higher，不說 more high。

p5.q: Overnight air, the ______ of the three shipping options, is used only for urgent medical supplies.
p5.exp: of the three（三者之中）要用最高級：the costliest（最貴的）。costlier 和 more costly 是比較級，用於兩者比較；costly 是原級，前面加 the 又接 of the three 不合文法。

p5.q: We look forward to ______ with your procurement team on the next phase of the warehouse expansion.
p5.exp: look forward to（期待）的 to 是介係詞，後面接動名詞 working。work、be working、have worked 都是把 to 誤當成不定詞的常見錯誤。

p5.q: After two years at the Singapore office, Mr. Haddad is accustomed to ______ calls with clients in several time zones.
p5.exp: be accustomed to（習慣於）的 to 是介係詞，後面接動名詞 handling。handle、have handled 是把 to 當成不定詞；be handled 是被動，變成 Haddad 被處理，意思不對。

p5.q: Smaller retailers cannot afford ______ large inventories of seasonal goods that may not sell.
p5.exp: afford（負擔得起）後面接不定詞：cannot afford to keep。afford 不接動名詞 keeping 或 having kept，也不能直接接原形 keep。

p5.q: The finance director has decided to delay ______ the new expense software until the year-end closing is complete.
p5.exp: delay（延後）後面接動名詞：delay introducing。前面的 decided to 已經用掉不定詞，這裡容易被誤導選 to introduce；introduce 是原形；introduced 是過去式或過去分詞，不能當 delay 的受詞。

p5.q: The newly hired sales associates are eager ______ their product training so that they can start meeting clients.
p5.exp: be eager to + 原形動詞（渴望做某事）：are eager to complete。eager 後面不接動名詞 completing，也不接原形 complete；for completing 也不對：be eager for 後面接名詞（eager for success），不接帶受詞的動名詞片語。

p5.q: Several board members objected to ______ the annual sales conference from Lisbon to a smaller regional venue.
p5.exp: object to（反對）的 to 是介係詞，後面接動名詞：objected to moving。move、have moved 是把 to 當成不定詞；be moved 是被動，但後面有受詞 the annual sales conference，要用主動。

p5.q: To meet the new emission targets, the plant will stop ______ coal-fired boilers by the end of 2027.
p5.exp: stop + V-ing 是「停止做某事」；stop + to V 是「停下來去做另一件事」。為了符合減排目標，工廠是要停止使用燃煤鍋爐，所以用 using。to use 意思變成「停下來去使用」，和減排矛盾；use、used 不能接在 stop 後面當受詞。

p5.q: Please remember ______ your parking permit to the security desk when you leave the facility on Friday.
p5.exp: remember + to V 是「記得要去做（還沒做）」；remember + V-ing 是「記得做過（已經做了）」。週五離開時才要歸還，是未來要做的事，用 to return。returning 指記得已經還過；return、returned 不能接在 remember 後面。

p5.q: The proposed delivery window was too narrow for the carrier ______ without hiring additional drivers.
p5.exp: too + 形容詞 + for + 人 + to V 表示「對某人來說太……而無法做」：too narrow for the carrier to accept。accepting、accept、accepted 都不能放進這個句型。

p5.q: The extended warranty is well worth ______ for any café that runs its espresso machines more than ten hours a day.
p5.exp: be worth + V-ing 表示「值得做某事」：is well worth purchasing。worth 後面不接不定詞 to purchase；purchase 若當名詞要加冠詞（worth the purchase），這裡沒有冠詞；purchased 是過去分詞，不能接在 worth 後面。

p5.q: In addition to ______ the company's payroll, Ms. Mbeki oversees benefits enrollment for all 600 employees.
p5.exp: in addition to（除了……之外）的 to 是介係詞，後面接動名詞 managing。manage、be managing 是把 to 誤當成不定詞；managed 是過去式或過去分詞，不能當介係詞的受詞。

p5.q: The hospitality team spent most of the morning ______ the ballroom for the evening's awards dinner.
p5.exp: spend + 時間 + V-ing 表示「花時間做某事」：spent most of the morning preparing。spend 後面不接不定詞 to prepare，也不接原形 prepare；prepared 是被動意思，變成團隊被準備，不合邏輯。

p5.q: The final assembly cost was nearly double ______ the engineering team had originally estimated.
p5.exp: 空格前沒有先行詞，空格後的子句 the engineering team had originally estimated 缺受詞，要用本身含先行詞的複合關係代名詞 what（= the amount that，……所估計的金額）。which、that 前面都需要先行詞；whatever 是「不論什麼」，意思不符。

p5.q: The guest survey measured the extent ______ visitors were satisfied with the hotel's new self-service check-in kiosks.
p5.exp: 固定說法 to the extent / the extent to which（到什麼程度）：the extent to which visitors were satisfied（旅客滿意的程度）。which 單獨使用時後面子句必須缺主詞或受詞，但 visitors were satisfied 是完整子句；in that 是「因為」的意思；whereby 是「藉此」，都和 extent 不搭。

p5.q: Ms. Sorensen asked the shipping agent to describe the conditions ______ the cargo had been stored before it reached the port.
p5.exp: under ... conditions（在……條件下）是固定搭配，介係詞移到關係代名詞前面形成 under which，後面接完整子句 the cargo had been stored。which 單獨使用時後面要缺主詞或受詞；whom 指人；whose 後面必須接名詞。

p5.q: The two hotels signed an agreement ______ guests of either property may use the other's fitness facilities free of charge.
p5.exp: whereby（依此、根據此協議）是關係副詞，先行詞 agreement，後面接完整子句：an agreement whereby guests ... may use。whereas 是表對比的連接詞（然而）；wherever 是「無論何處」；whether 是「是否」，都無法修飾 agreement。

p5.q: Rising fuel costs are the main reason ______ the airline has reduced the number of weekly flights to Dublin.
p5.exp: 先行詞是 reason，後面是完整子句，用關係副詞 why（= for which）。which 後面的子句要缺主詞或受詞；what 前面不能有先行詞；how 是表方法，和 reason 不搭。

p5.q: Customers may choose ______ delivery option best suits their schedule at no additional cost.
p5.exp: 空格後直接接名詞 delivery option，再接動詞 best suits，需要能當形容詞用的複合關係詞 whichever（無論哪一個）：whichever delivery option best suits。whoever 指人，不能修飾名詞；wherever 指地點；however 是「無論如何」，後面接形容詞或副詞。

p5.q: The only supplier ______ could guarantee delivery within ten days was a small packaging firm in Porto.
p5.exp: 先行詞前有 the only 時，關係代名詞常用 that，而且空格後缺主詞（___ could guarantee），要主格：that。what 前面不能有先行詞；whose 後面必須接名詞；whom 是受格，不能當主詞。

p5.q: The firm hired forty seasonal workers, most of ______ had previous experience in fruit processing.
p5.exp: 「數量詞 + of + 關係代名詞」：most of whom（其中大多數人）。介係詞 of 後面指人要用受格 whom。them 是人稱代名詞，用 them 會變成兩個子句沒有連接詞，文法錯誤；who 是主格，不能放在 of 後面；which 指物，不能指 workers。

p5.q: The applicant ______ the hiring committee believes is best qualified will be contacted by phone on Friday.
p5.exp: the hiring committee believes 是插入語，拿掉後是 The applicant ___ is best qualified，空格當 is 的主詞，用主格 who。whom 是受格，是最常見的陷阱（誤以為是 believes 的受詞）；whose 後面要接名詞；which 不指人。

p5.q: Inventory will be counted on November 30, ______ all three warehouses will be closed to outside deliveries.
p5.exp: 先行詞是日期 November 30，後面接完整子句，用表示時間的關係副詞 when（逗號後補充說明）。which 後面子句要缺主詞或受詞；where 用於地點；whom 指人。

p5.q: ______ the new loading bays are fully operational, trucks rarely wait more than fifteen minutes to unload.
p5.exp: Now that（既然、由於現在）引導原因子句，意思是新卸貨區已全面運作，所以卡車幾乎不用等。Even if（即使）是讓步，和語意相反；In case of 是介係詞片語，後面只能接名詞；As though（彷彿）意思不通。

p5.q: Keep a printed copy of the guest list at the front desk ______ the reservation system goes offline during the gala.
p5.exp: in case + 子句 表示「以防萬一……」，後面 the reservation system goes offline 是完整子句，用連接詞 in case。in case of 是介係詞片語，後面只能接名詞；as if（好像）意思不通；so as 要接 to V（so as to）。

p5.q: The Toronto office handles large corporate accounts, ______ the Montreal branch focuses mainly on small businesses.
p5.exp: 前後兩個子句做對比（多倫多處理大企業、蒙特婁專注小企業），要用表對比的連接詞 whereas（然而、反之）。despite、unlike 是介係詞，後面只能接名詞，不能接子句；otherwise 是副詞（否則），不能連接兩個子句，意思也不對。

p5.q: ______ a last-minute change in flour suppliers, the bakery chain launched its holiday menu on schedule.
p5.exp: 空格後是名詞片語 a last-minute change，不是子句，要用介係詞 Notwithstanding（儘管）。Even though、Whereas 是連接詞，後面必須接子句；Nevertheless 是副詞（然而），不能直接接名詞。這題考連接詞與介係詞之分。

p5.q: The hotel received ______ positive reviews that it was named the region's top boutique property.
p5.exp: such + 形容詞 + 名詞 + that 表示「如此……以致於」：such positive reviews that。so 後面直接接形容詞或副詞（so positive that），中間不能夾名詞 reviews；too、very 無法和 that 子句構成結果句型。

p5.q: Ms. Desai recommended leasing the forklifts ______ buying them outright, since demand may fall after the holiday season.
p5.exp: rather than 連接兩個對等的動名詞 leasing 和 buying：建議租賃而不是買斷。instead 是副詞，要用 instead of 才能接 buying；other than 是「除了」，意思不通；in place 要用 in place of。

p5.q: Overtime will be paid ______ it has been approved in advance by a department supervisor.
p5.exp: only if（唯有在……時）引導條件：加班要事先核准才會支付。unless（除非）會變成「沒核准才付錢」，意思相反；even so 是副詞（即使如此），不能引導子句；in order that 是「為了」，意思不通。

p5.q: Production of the older model will continue ______ the new assembly line is being installed next door.
p5.exp: 空格後是完整子句 the new assembly line is being installed，要用連接詞 while（當……的時候）。during、throughout 是介係詞，只能接名詞；meanwhile 是副詞（同時），不能連接兩個子句。

p5.q: ______ the warehouse lease expires in March, the operations team has already started searching for a new site.
p5.exp: Given that（考慮到、既然）是連接詞，後面接完整子句，說明開始找新地點的原因。Owing to、In spite of 是介係詞，只能接名詞；Such as（例如）用來舉例，不能引導子句。

p5.q: The printer jammed repeatedly during the morning shift, ______ the brochures were not ready for the trade show.
p5.exp: 逗號後要連接兩個完整子句，需要對等連接詞 so（所以）。therefore、consequently、as a result 雖然意思相同，但它們是副詞（片語），不能只用逗號連接兩個子句，要改用分號或句號才行。

p5.q: Ms. Abara accepted the hospitality award ______ the entire housekeeping staff at last night's ceremony.
p5.exp: on behalf of（代表）：代表整個房務團隊領獎。in favor of 是「支持、贊成」；by means of 是「藉由（某種手段）」；in place 要用 in place of 才能接名詞，而且意思是「取代」，都不符語意。

p5.q: All hazardous materials must be labeled ______ the guidelines issued by the regional safety authority.
p5.exp: in accordance with（依照）是固定片語。in compliance to 錯在要搭配 with（in compliance with）；with regard of 錯在要搭配 to（with regard to）；in respect for 不是正確片語（應為 in respect of 或 out of respect for）。

p5.q: ______ November 1, reimbursement claims will no longer be accepted on paper forms.
p5.exp: As of + 日期 表示「自……起（生效）」：自 11 月 1 日起不再收紙本。Since 要搭配完成式，不能接未來式 will；Until 意思是「直到……為止」，和 no longer 搭起來語意矛盾；Among 用在三者以上的群體之間。

p5.q: Shipping rates rose sharply ______ growing demand for container space ahead of the holiday season.
p5.exp: amid（在……的情勢下、伴隨著）後面接情況或事件：amid growing demand（在需求增加之際）。among 後面接複數的人或物；between 用於兩者之間；along 是「沿著」，都不符語意。

p5.q: Suppliers may receive early payment ______ a two percent discount on the invoice total.
p5.exp: in exchange for（以……作為交換）：供應商給 2% 折扣來換取提早付款。in return of 應為 in return for；by way to 應為 by way of；instead for 應為 instead of，這三個都是介係詞搭錯的常見錯誤。

p5.q: The delay was caused by circumstances ______ the carrier's control, so no penalty will be charged.
p5.exp: beyond one's control（無法控制的）是固定說法，所以運送商不必受罰。against 是「違反、反對」；past 表時間或位置的經過；without 是「沒有」，都和 control 搭不出「超出控制」的意思。

p5.q: All shipments leaving the Antwerp facility are insured ______ loss or damage during transit.
p5.exp: insure against（投保以防……）是固定搭配：投保防範遺失或損壞。from、about、toward 都不能和 insure 搭配表示「防範風險」。

p5.q: ______ a few minor scratches on the casing, the returned laptops were in excellent condition.
p5.exp: Apart from（除了……之外）：除了外殼上的小刮痕，退回的筆電狀況極佳。Instead of 是「代替」；Due to 是「因為」，刮痕不會造成狀況極佳；Along with 是「連同」，和後面的 excellent condition 語意矛盾。

p5.q: The east parking lot will remain unavailable ______ the duration of the resurfacing project.
p5.exp: for the duration of（在……的整個期間）是固定說法。to 不能表示一段期間；within 是「在……之內」，搭配 the duration 不自然；since 要接過去的起點並搭配完成式。

p5.q: The new bottling line fills containers ______ a rate of nearly 400 per minute.
p5.exp: at a rate of（以……的速度）是固定搭配。in、by、with 都不和 rate of 搭配表示速度。

p5.q: The number of guests requesting late checkout ______ nearly doubled since the hotel introduced its mobile app.
p5.exp: 主詞是 The number（……的數目），是單數，所以用 has；加上 since 子句，要現在完成式 has doubled。容易被 guests 誤導選 have；are、were 加上 doubled 變成被動或時態錯誤。注意 A number of + 複數名詞才用複數動詞。

p5.q: The plant manager, along with two senior engineers, ______ expected to attend the safety review in Osaka next week.
p5.exp: along with（連同）引導的片語是插入語，不影響主詞的單複數，真正主詞是 The plant manager（單數），所以用 is。are、were、have been 都是複數動詞；而且 next week 是未來，were 時態也不對。

p5.q: Every invoice and every receipt submitted after the deadline ______ to be reviewed by the financial controller.
p5.exp: Every A and every B 作主詞時，動詞仍用單數，因為 every 強調逐一個別看待：needs。need、are needing、have needed 都是複數形式；而且 need 表示需要時通常不用進行式。

p5.q: The list of approved vendors for office furniture and equipment ______ updated at the start of each fiscal year.
p5.exp: 主詞是 The list（名單，單數），of approved vendors ... equipment 只是修飾語，所以用 is。are、were 被中間的 vendors 誤導成複數；have updated 是主動，名單不會自己更新，而且也是複數形。

p5.q: Either the regional managers or the operations director ______ responsible for approving emergency purchases.
p5.exp: Either A or B 的動詞要和靠近動詞的 B 一致（就近原則）。B 是 the operations director（單數），所以用 is。are、were、have been 都是複數，被前面的 managers 誤導。

p5.q: Reducing delivery times while keeping shipping costs low ______ the top priority for the logistics team this year.
p5.exp: 動名詞片語 Reducing delivery times ... low 當主詞時視為單數，所以用 remains。容易被 times、costs 這些複數名詞誤導選 remain、have remained；are remaining 也是複數，且 remain 通常不用進行式。

p5.q: Ms. Varga is one of the analysts who ______ responsible for preparing the quarterly cost forecasts.
p5.exp: one of the + 複數名詞 + who 時，關係代名詞 who 的先行詞是 the analysts（複數），所以動詞用 are（她是那些負責預測的分析師之一）。is、has been 誤把先行詞當成 one；was 是單數且時態不對。

p5.q: Roughly half of the shipment ______ damaged by seawater when the container was dropped at the port.
p5.exp: half of + 名詞 的動詞單複數看 of 後面的名詞：the shipment（這批貨）是單數，所以用單數；when 子句是過去式，用 was。were、have been、are 都是複數動詞；are 時態也不對。

p5.q: ______ you require further assistance with your booking, please contact our reservations desk at any time.
p5.exp: Should you require ... = If you should require ...（萬一您需要……），省略 if 並把 should 移到主詞前面，是商務書信常見的倒裝。Would 不能這樣倒裝成條件句；Had 後面要接過去分詞；Were 後面要接 to V 或形容詞，不能接原形 require。

p5.q: ______ the board to approve the expansion, construction of the new plant would begin next spring.
p5.exp: Were + 主詞 + to V = If + 主詞 + were to V，表示對未來的假設，主要子句用 would begin。空格後是 to approve，只有 Were 能接；Had 後面要接過去分詞；Should 後面要接原形（Should the board approve），不接 to；Did 不能用在這種倒裝。

p5.q: ______ the supplier informed us of the price increase earlier, we would have placed a larger order in August.
p5.exp: 主要子句 would have placed 是與過去事實相反的假設，條件子句要過去完成式 If the supplier had informed，省略 if 後倒裝成 Had the supplier informed。If the supplier informed 是過去式，和 would have placed 搭配不上；Should、Were 都不能和過去分詞 informed 構成這種倒裝。

p5.q: It is imperative that the new head chef ______ certified in food safety before he starts working in the hotel kitchen.
p5.exp: It is imperative / essential / vital that + 主詞 + (should) + 原形動詞，這是表示必要的假設語氣，即使主詞是第三人稱單數也用原形 be。is、will be 是直述語氣，不符合這個句型；being 不能當子句的動詞。

p5.q: The client insisted that its logo ______ altered in any way on the printed packaging.
p5.exp: insist（堅持要求）後面的 that 子句用原形動詞，否定時 not 放在原形前面：(should) not be altered。not being 不能當子句的動詞；does not altered、has not altered 文法錯誤，而且標誌是「被」修改，要被動。

p5.q: Rarely ______ a new product line generated as much customer interest as the company's compostable coffee pods.
p5.exp: 否定副詞 Rarely 放在句首時，後面要倒裝成「助動詞 + 主詞 + 動詞」：Rarely has a new product line generated。it has 是沒有倒裝的語序，而且多了 it；主詞 a new product line 是單數，不能用 have；having 不是助動詞，無法倒裝。

p5.q: So great ______ for the limited-edition handbags that the boutique sold out within two hours of opening.
p5.exp: So + 形容詞 放在句首強調時，後面要倒裝成「be 動詞 + 主詞」：So great was the demand that ...（需求大到……）。the demand was、demand was 沒有倒裝；did the demand 後面缺動詞，而且 great 是形容詞，要搭配 be 動詞而不是 did。

p5.q: Under no circumstances ______ to share their login credentials with contractors or temporary staff.
p5.exp: 否定片語 Under no circumstances（無論如何都不）放句首時，主詞和 be 動詞要倒裝：are employees permitted。employees are permitted 是一般語序；permitted are employees 把分詞放到最前面，語序錯誤；employees permitted 缺少 be 動詞。

p5.q: The new inventory software can reorder low-stock items ______, without any input from the purchasing staff.
p5.exp: by itself（自己、獨自地）表示不需要別人協助，和後面的 without any input 呼應。itself by 語序錯誤；by its own 不是正確說法（應為 on its own）；on itself 不能表示「獨力」。

p5.q: Two of the five delivery trucks passed inspection, but ______ will need new brakes before returning to service.
p5.exp: 五輛中兩輛通過，剩下的三輛是特定的「其餘全部」，用 the others（複數代名詞），搭配 will need。another 是「另一個（不特定的一個）」；the other 指兩者中剩下的那一個（單數），但這裡剩三輛；other 是形容詞，後面要接名詞，不能單獨當主詞。

p5.q: The new warehouse's storage capacity is nearly double ______ of the old facility on Mill Road.
p5.exp: 為了避免重複前面的單數名詞 storage capacity，用 that of（……的那個）。those 用來代替複數名詞；it 和 this 不能接 of 來代替前面提過的名詞。

p5.q: The Meridian Hotel's conference package costs less than ______, but it does not include any audiovisual equipment.
p5.exp: than 後面要比較的是「我們的方案」，用所有格代名詞 ours（= our conference package）。our 是所有格形容詞，後面必須接名詞；us 是受格，變成拿方案和「我們這些人」比較；ourselves 是反身代名詞，不能這樣用。

p5.q: ______ of the applicants for the sous-chef position had at least five years of restaurant experience.
p5.exp: Most of the + 複數名詞（大部分的……）。Almost 是副詞，不能直接接 of（要說 Almost all of）；Every 不能接 of（要用 Every one of 或 Each of）；Much of 用於不可數名詞，applicants 是可數複數。

p5.q: Ms. Brennan's sales figures for the third quarter were higher than ______ on the regional team.
p5.exp: 要拿「她的業績」和「團隊中其他任何人的業績」比較，必須用所有格；anyone else 的所有格是把 's 加在 else 後面：anyone else's。anyone's else、else anyone's 語序錯誤；anyone else 沒有所有格，變成拿業績和「人」比較，不對等。

p5.q: The new booking system makes ______ possible for guests to change their reservations without calling the front desk.
p5.exp: make + it + 形容詞 + for 人 + to V：it 是虛受詞，代替後面真正的受詞 to change their reservations。this 不能當虛受詞；them 是複數，找不到可以指的對象；what 不能放在受詞位置構成這個句型。

p5.q: The regional director asked Ms. Okoro and ______ to prepare a summary of the third-quarter freight costs.
p5.exp: asked 後面的受詞是 Ms. Okoro and ___，受詞位置要用受格 me。I 是主格，是常見錯誤（以為「and I」比較禮貌）；myself 是反身代名詞，只有主詞也是「我」時才能用；mine 是所有格代名詞，意思是「我的東西」。

p5.q: ______ the annual inventory audit, the warehouse staff were given an extra day off.
p5.exp: 分詞構句的主詞和主要子句相同（the warehouse staff），員工是「完成」盤點的一方，要主動；而且完成盤點發生在放假之前，用完成式分詞 Having completed。Completed 和 Having been completed 是被動，變成員工被完成；To have completed 表示目的或推測，意思不通。

p5.q: When ______ properly, the new air filters can last up to eighteen months without replacement.
p5.exp: When (they are) maintained properly：省略了主詞和 be 動詞，濾網是「被維護」的，用過去分詞 maintained。maintaining 是主動，變成濾網去維護別的東西；maintain 是原形動詞，不能直接接在 When 後面；maintenance 是名詞，不能被副詞 properly 修飾。

p5.q: Despite the delays, the client remained ______ with the overall progress of the lobby renovation.
p5.exp: remain 是連綴動詞，後面要形容詞；客戶是「感到滿意」的人，用過去分詞 satisfied，搭配 with。satisfying 是「令人滿意的」，用來形容事物；satisfaction 是名詞，不能接 with 表示感受；satisfactorily 是副詞，不能當補語。

p5.q: The contract ______, the two firms began joint production of the new electric scooters in March.
p5.exp: 這是獨立分詞構句：前半句的主詞 The contract 和主要子句的主詞 the two firms 不同，所以保留下來。合約是「被簽署」，而且簽約發生在開始生產之前，用完成式被動分詞 having been signed。having signed、signing 是主動，合約不會去簽別的東西；to sign 表示目的，語意不通。

p5.q: Bellmont Suites, ______ just two blocks from the convention center, offers discounted rates to registered attendees.
p5.exp: be located（位於）是被動說法，省略 which is 後留下過去分詞 located 修飾 Bellmont Suites。locating 是主動，意思變成「去找出位置」；locates 是動詞，句子已經有動詞 offers，不能再多一個；location 是名詞，不能接 just two blocks from。

p5.q: Any packaging material ______ hazardous substances must be disposed of separately from regular waste.
p5.exp: 空格後有受詞 hazardous substances，要用現在分詞 containing（= which contains）修飾 material，表示「含有……的」。contained 是被動，後面不能再接受詞；contains、contain 是動詞，句子已經有動詞 must be disposed，不能再多一個動詞。

p5.q: Unless otherwise ______, all prices listed in the catalog include delivery within the metropolitan area.
p5.exp: Unless otherwise stated（除非另有說明）是固定說法，等於 Unless it is otherwise stated，事情是「被說明」，用過去分詞 stated。stating 是主動；statement 是名詞，不能被副詞 otherwise 修飾；states 是動詞，前面沒有主詞。

p5.q: ______ costs for raw materials have forced several furniture manufacturers to raise their prices.
p5.exp: rise（上升）是不及物動詞，現在分詞 Rising 當形容詞修飾 costs，表示「不斷上升的成本」。Risen 是過去分詞，不及物動詞的過去分詞不能這樣當形容詞表被動；Rose 是過去式動詞；Raise 是及物動詞原形（提高），不能放在名詞前當形容詞。

p5.q: The revised overtime policy is intended to ______ employees' concerns about unpaid work on weekends.
p5.exp: address concerns 是「處理、回應疑慮」，政策的目的是解決員工對週末無薪工作的擔憂，所以選 address。raise、voice、express concerns 都是「提出、表達疑慮」，那是員工做的事，不是政策要達成的目的。

p5.q: Customers who return their rental vans after 6 P.M. will be ______ an additional fee of 25 euros.
p5.exp: charge + 人 + 費用（向某人收取費用），被動是 人 + be charged + 費用：晚還車的顧客會被收 25 歐元。be paid a fee 是「收到款項」，意思相反；spend 的主詞是付錢的人，不能說 be spent a fee；priced 來自 price（定價），不能接人當受詞。

p5.q: The packaging supplier offers a volume ______ to customers who order more than 500 units per month.
p5.exp: volume discount（大量訂購折扣）是固定的商業用語：訂購量大就給折扣。deduction 多指扣除額（稅務或薪資）；decline 是「下降」；subtraction 是數學的「減法」，都不能和 volume 搭配表示購買優惠。

p5.q: The product launch drew ______ coverage from both national newspapers and industry magazines.
p5.exp: extensive coverage（廣泛的報導）是常見搭配。spacious、roomy 指空間寬敞，用來形容房間或車子；numerous 是「許多的」，要修飾可數複數名詞，coverage 是不可數名詞。

p5.q: Due to a scheduling ______, Mr. Mensah will be unable to attend Thursday's budget review.
p5.exp: scheduling conflict（行程衝突、撞期）是固定搭配。dispute、argument、quarrel 都有「爭執、爭吵」的意思，但指人和人之間的衝突，不能和 scheduling 搭配表示時間撞在一起。

p5.q: The new catering contract ______ that all deliveries be made between 6 A.M. and 10 A.M.
p5.exp: stipulates that（明文規定）用於合約條款，後面接原形動詞 be made。persuades、convinces、reminds 都要先接「人」當受詞（persuade someone that），不能直接接 that 子句，而且合約無法說服或提醒。

p5.q: Employees must ______ their supervisors at least two weeks before taking extended leave.
p5.exp: notify + 人（通知某人）：員工要提前通知主管。announce、mention、declare 的受詞是「事情」而不是「人」，要說 announce something to someone，不能說 announce their supervisors。

p5.q: The finance director gave a ______ estimate of next year's costs, assuming fuel prices will rise sharply.
p5.exp: conservative estimate 是「保守的估計」，也就是預留空間、往不利方向估，正好對應「假設油價大漲」。traditional、conventional、old-fashioned 都有「傳統、守舊」的意思，但不能形容估計數字的謹慎程度。

p5.q: The resort's greatest ______ is its location within walking distance of the historic old town.
p5.exp: asset 除了「資產」，也可以指「優勢、長處」：度假村最大的優勢是地點。ownership 是「所有權」；belonging 單數是「歸屬感」，指物品要用複數 belongings；possession 是「擁有物」，都不能表示「優點」。

p5.q: The CEO's ______ remarks at the start of the meeting set a positive tone for the negotiations.
p5.exp: opening remarks（開場致詞）是固定搭配。starting 雖然也有「開始」的意思，但不和 remarks 搭配；initiating 指發起某項行動；launching 指推出產品或發起活動，都不能形容致詞。

p5.q: Please ______ that all loading doors are locked before leaving the warehouse at night.
p5.exp: ensure that（確保）後面直接接 that 子句：確保所有門都鎖好。assure、reassure 是「向某人保證、使某人安心」，要先接人當受詞（assure someone that）；secure 是「取得、固定」，不接 that 子句。

p5.q: The annual marketing budget was ______ among the four regional teams according to last year's sales.
p5.exp: allocated（分配資源、預算）常和 among 搭配：預算依去年銷售分配給四個團隊。appointed、nominated 是「任命、提名」人；designated 是「指定、指派」某人或某物作特定用途，都不搭配 among 來表示分配金錢。

p5.q: The new uniform policy tries to ______ a balance between a professional appearance and staff comfort.
p5.exp: strike a balance between A and B（在 A 和 B 之間取得平衡）是固定搭配。hit、beat 雖然和 strike 都有「打」的意思，但不能和 balance 搭配；make a balance 也不是英文的慣用說法。

p5.q: The airline plans to ______ its older aircraft by 2029 and replace them with more fuel-efficient models.
p5.exp: phase out（逐步淘汰）：舊飛機要逐步退役，再換成省油機型。phase in 是「逐步引進」，意思相反；carry out 是「執行（計畫、任務）」；take over 是「接管」，都和 replace them 的語意不符。

p5.q: Mr. Quintero will ______ Ms. Holloway at the reception desk while she attends the training seminar.
p5.exp: fill in for + 人（暫時代替某人工作）：她去受訓時由他代班。fill out 是「填寫（表格）」；fill up with 是「用……裝滿」；fill in on 用於 fill someone in on something，是「向某人說明某事」，後面要接事情，都不符語意。

p5.q: The legal department has been asked to ______ a new service contract for the catering supplier.
p5.exp: draw up a contract（草擬合約）是固定搭配。draw out 是「拉長、引出」；look up 是「查詢」；turn up 是「出現、調大音量」，都不能和 contract 搭配表示起草。

p5.q: The café usually ______ its signature sourdough by noon on Saturdays, so customers are advised to arrive early.
p5.exp: runs out of（用完、賣完）：中午前招牌麵包就賣光，所以建議早點來。runs into 是「偶遇、碰上（問題）」；runs over 是「輾過、超過時間」；runs across 是「偶然發現」，都和 so customers are advised to arrive early 的因果關係不符。

p5.q: Restaurant managers must ______ orders for fresh produce no later than 3 P.M. on the day before delivery.
p5.exp: place an order（下訂單）是固定搭配。put、set、lay 雖然都有「放置」的意思，但不能和 order 搭配表示訂貨。

p5.q: The revised budget fails to ______ the rising cost of fuel for the company's delivery fleet.
p5.exp: take into account（將……納入考量）：修正後的預算沒有考慮到油價上漲。bring into play 是「使發揮作用」；put into effect 是「實施（政策）」；come into force 是「（法規）生效」，是不及物用法，後面不能接受詞。

p5.q: The customer service team promised to ______ the billing error and respond within two business days.
p5.exp: look into（調查、查明）：客服承諾調查帳單錯誤再回覆。look after 是「照顧」；look up to 是「尊敬」；look forward to 是「期待」，都和 billing error 搭配不起來。

SEATTLE (March 9) — Corvane Logistics announced today that it has entered into a three-year agreement with Northwind Air Cargo. Under the partnership, Corvane customers will gain access to overnight freight service between Seattle and twelve cities in Asia. ___[1]___, Northwind will dedicate two aircraft exclusively to Corvane shipments during the peak holiday season.

"Our clients have been asking for faster international options for some time," said Corvane CEO Marcus Webb. "This agreement allows us to meet that demand without ___[2]___ our own fleet of aircraft." ___[3]___

The new service will be available to customers beginning May 1. Corvane expects its international shipping volume to grow by 30 percent in the first year, and the company plans to hire forty additional warehouse employees to handle the ___[4]___ workload.

blanks.exp: 前一句說客戶可以使用隔夜空運服務，這句再補充另一項合作內容（旺季專用兩架飛機），是「追加」關係，用 In addition（此外）。Instead（反而）表示取代前面的內容；Even so（即便如此）表示讓步；Otherwise（否則）表示條件相反，都和前後文的關係不合。
介係詞 without 後面要接動名詞，而且後面還有受詞 our own fleet，所以用 expanding（擴充）。expand 是原形動詞、expanded 是過去式或過去分詞，都不能直接放在介係詞後面；expansion 是名詞，後面不能再直接接受詞 our own fleet。

opts: Until now, Corvane has shipped to Asia only by sea.
Northwind recently ended all of its cargo flights to Asian cities.
Mr. Webb founded the company with his brother in 1994.
Corvane also reported lower profits for the third quarter in a row.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：Webb 執行長剛說客戶一直要求「更快的國際運送選項」，接著補充背景「到目前為止只能走海運」，說明為什麼需要空運，最連貫。「Northwind 停飛所有亞洲航線」和第一段的亞洲十二個城市隔夜服務矛盾；公司創立年份、連續三季獲利下滑都和這次合作無關，放在這裡很突兀。
前面說國際運量預計成長 30%，所以要多僱四十名倉儲人員來處理「增加的」工作量：the increased workload。reduced（減少的）和運量成長矛盾；previous（先前的）工作量不需要新增人手；optional（可選擇的）和 workload 搭配不合理。

p6.title: 電子郵件：供應商調整價格
p6.text:
To: Purchasing Team, Delmont Furniture
From: Aisha Kamara, Account Manager, Teakwood Timber Supply
Date: August 3
Subject: Updated price list

Dear Purchasing Team,

I am writing to inform you of a change to our pricing. Due to rising transportation costs, the price of all hardwood products will increase by six percent ___[1]___ September 1. Orders placed before that date will be billed at current rates, even if they are delivered later.

We understand that this news may affect your production budget. ___[2]___ To help ease the transition, we are offering a one-time discount of four percent on any order of more than 500 board feet placed during August.

The updated price list is attached. Please note that softwood and plywood prices will remain ___[3]___ for the rest of the year.

___[4]___, we value our long relationship with Delmont Furniture and remain committed to delivering quality materials on schedule.

Sincerely,
Aisha Kamara

blanks.exp: effective + 日期＝「自某日起生效」，是公告價格、規定時的固定用法：will increase … effective September 1（9 月 1 日起調漲）。effectively 是副詞（有效地／實際上），不能接日期；effects 是名詞複數或第三人稱動詞；effected 是過去分詞（被實現），放在這裡都不通。

opts: We have worked hard to keep this increase as small as possible.
Hardwood prices have fallen steadily over the past year.
Your most recent shipment was delivered two days late.
Our warehouse will be closed for the entire month of August.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：前一句說「這個消息可能影響貴公司的預算」，接著說「我們已盡力把漲幅壓到最低」，再接 To help ease the transition 提出折扣，語氣一路連貫。「硬木價格持續下跌」和信中說成本上升、要漲價矛盾；上一批貨晚到兩天和漲價無關；「倉庫八月整月關閉」和後面「八月下單享折扣」矛盾。
Please note 這句是在對比：硬木漲價，但軟木和夾板價格「維持不變」，remain unchanged。unfinished（未完成的）、unattended（無人看管的）、unopened（未開封的）都不能用來形容價格。
最後一段是結尾，不論前面說了漲價這類壞消息，都要強調重視雙方的長期合作，用 In any case（無論如何）。As a result（因此）會變成「因為漲價，所以我們重視合作」，因果不通；For example（例如）後面沒有舉例；Otherwise（否則）需要前面有條件，這裡沒有。

p6.title: 公告：大樓消防演習
p6.text:
NOTICE TO ALL TENANTS

The annual fire drill for the Prescott Building will take place on Wednesday, April 15, at approximately 10:30 A.M. When the alarm sounds, all occupants must leave the building by the nearest stairway. Elevators will be ___[1]___ automatically and must not be used.

Once outside, please proceed to your assigned assembly area in the north parking lot. Floor wardens will check that everyone ___[2]___ accounted for before the all-clear signal is given. ___[3]___

The drill is required by city regulations and is designed to ensure that all occupants know how to respond in a real emergency. ___[4]___, we ask tenants to inform their visitors and clients of the drill in advance.

blanks.exp: 後面說電梯「不得使用」，所以前面是電梯會被自動「停用」：will be disabled automatically。dismissed 用在人（解散、解僱）；discarded 是丟棄；displaced 是移位、使流離失所，都不適合描述演習時的電梯。
that 子句需要一個完整的動詞，主詞 everyone 是單數，所以用 has been accounted for（都已清點到）。have been 是複數動詞，和 everyone 不一致；being 和 to be 都不是完整的動詞，that 子句會缺少動詞。

opts: The whole drill should take about twenty minutes.
Employees on the ground floor may remain at their desks.
Visitors must sign in at the security desk upon arrival.
The north parking lot will be repaved later this spring.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：前一句說到解除警報（all-clear signal）為止的流程，接著說明整個演習「大約二十分鐘」，是對流程的總結，最連貫。「一樓員工可以留在座位」和第一段 all occupants must leave 矛盾；訪客簽到和演習無關；停車場之後要重鋪是另一件事，放在這裡離題。
請房客事先告訴訪客和客戶有演習，目的是「避免混亂」，用 To avoid confusion（為了避免混淆）。In contrast（相對地）需要前後對比；Even so（即便如此）需要讓步關係；Instead（取而代之）表示替換，都和前一句「演習是法規要求、為了讓大家知道如何應變」接不起來。

p6.title: 廣告：辦公室植栽租賃
p6.text:
Bring Your Workspace to Life with GreenLease

Studies show that plants can reduce stress and improve concentration in the workplace. But keeping them healthy takes time that busy professionals simply do not have. That is ___[1]___ GreenLease comes in.

For a low monthly fee, our designers will select plants suited to the light and temperature conditions of your office. ___[2]___ Our technicians then visit every two weeks to water, trim, and fertilize each plant. If a plant ___[3]___ to thrive, we will replace it at no extra charge.

GreenLease currently serves more than 400 businesses in the Denver area. ___[4]___, new clients who sign a twelve-month agreement before June 30 will receive their first month free. Call 555-0187 to schedule a free consultation.

blanks.exp: That is where … comes in 是固定說法，意思是「這就是某某派上用場的地方」，where 是關係副詞，後面接完整子句 GreenLease comes in。which、whom 是關係代名詞，後面子句要缺受詞或主詞，但 GreenLease comes in 已經完整；what 也一樣需要子句缺一個名詞，句子都不通。

opts: They will also deliver the plants and arrange them for you.
Artificial plants are a popular low-cost alternative.
You will need to water each plant twice a week.
Most of our plants are grown in greenhouses abroad.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：前一句說設計師幫你挑選植物，下一句用 then（接著）說技術人員每兩週來照顧，中間需要「送來並擺好」這個步驟，They 指設計師，最連貫。人造植物和這項租賃服務無關；「你要每週澆兩次水」和技術人員負責澆水矛盾；植物在國外溫室種植是離題資訊，也接不上 then。
fail to thrive＝長不好、無法存活，是描述植物（或生物）狀況的固定說法：如果植物長不好，免費換新。decline to 是「婉拒去做」，refuse to 是「拒絕去做」，都需要有意志的主詞；neglect to 是「疏忽沒做」，植物不會疏忽，三個都不合。
前一句說服務超過 400 家企業（優點），這句再加一個好處：新客戶簽約一年免第一個月費用，是追加關係，用 What's more（而且、更棒的是）。However 表示轉折，但前後沒有對立；Therefore 表示因果，「服務很多家企業」不會導致「新客戶免一個月」；Likewise（同樣地）需要前後是相似的情況。

p6.title: 備忘錄：新的訪客登記程序
p6.text:
MEMO
To: All Staff
From: Gregory Okafor, Head of Security
Date: February 16
Re: New visitor procedure

Beginning Monday, March 2, all visitors to our headquarters must be registered in advance through the VisitorPass system. Employees who are expecting a guest should enter the visitor's name, company, and expected arrival time no later than 5:00 P.M. on the previous business day. The system will then automatically ___[1]___ the guest an e-mail containing a QR code.

___[2]___ Unregistered visitors will be asked to wait in the lobby until their host comes down to sign them in personally.

This change is part of a wider effort to improve building security. ___[3]___, it will allow reception staff to prepare badges ahead of time, reducing waiting times at the front desk. A short guide to VisitorPass ___[4]___ to this memo. Please direct any questions to the security office at extension 4120.

blanks.exp: 空格後面是 the guest（人）＋ an e-mail（物）兩個受詞，只有 send 可以這樣用：send someone something（寄給某人某物）。inform 和 notify 的用法是 inform/notify someone of something，不能直接接 an e-mail；deliver 一般說 deliver something to someone，不接兩個受詞。

opts: Guests will need to show this code at the reception desk upon arrival.
Visitors will no longer be required to check in at reception.
The lobby will be closed for repainting throughout March.
Our headquarters first opened its doors to the public in 2011.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：前一段結尾提到系統寄出含 QR code 的電子郵件，這句用 this code 接著說「訪客抵達時要在櫃台出示」，後面再說沒登記的訪客要在大廳等候，前後呼應。「訪客不用再到櫃台報到」和新程序矛盾；「大廳三月整修關閉」和「未登記訪客在大廳等候」矛盾；總部開幕年份和訪客程序無關。
前一句說這項改變能提升大樓安全，這句再說另一個好處（櫃台可以先準備好識別證、縮短等候時間），是追加關係，用 In addition（此外）。Instead（反而）表示取代；Otherwise（否則）表示相反條件；Nonetheless（儘管如此）表示讓步，前後都沒有對立。
主詞是 A short guide（指南），指南是「被附上」的，要用被動語態 is attached to this memo。attaches 和 has attached 是主動，會變成「指南附上了某物」，而且後面沒有受詞；attaching 不是完整的動詞，句子缺少動詞。

p6.title: 信件：標案結果通知
p6.text:
Ridgeway Municipal Services
410 Harlan Avenue
Ridgeway

November 12

Ms. Priya Desai
Desai Landscaping
88 Orchard Lane
Ridgeway

Dear Ms. Desai,

Thank you for submitting a proposal to maintain the grounds of Ridgeway's public parks. We received eleven bids for this contract, and the selection committee reviewed each one ___[1]___.

After much consideration, we have decided to award the contract to another company. Your proposal was well organized, and your references spoke highly of your work. ___[2]___, the committee felt that the winning bid offered a more detailed plan for reducing water use, which is a priority for the city this year.

___[3]___ We will keep your company's information on file and would encourage you to bid on future projects. The next round of contracts, which ___[4]___ snow removal and street cleaning, will be announced in January.

Sincerely,
Thomas Reilly
Procurement Officer

blanks.exp: 句子 the committee reviewed each one 已經完整，空格要修飾動詞 reviewed，用副詞 carefully（仔細地）。careful 是形容詞，不能修飾動詞；care 是名詞或動詞；cared 是過去式，放在句尾都不通。
前一句稱讚對方提案條理分明、推薦人評價很高，這句卻說委員會認為得標者的省水計畫更詳細，是「先肯定、再轉折」，用 Nevertheless（儘管如此）。Therefore（因此）會變成「因為你的提案很好，所以別人得標」，因果不通；Likewise（同樣地）需要相似的情況；In other words（換句話說）需要前後意思相同。

opts: We realize that this news is disappointing.
Work will begin as soon as you sign the enclosed contract.
Our parks department plans to hire three gardeners in spring.
The committee will meet again next week to review the bids.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：前面說明沒有得標的原因，這段開頭先表達體諒「我們知道這個消息令人失望」，再接「會保留貴公司資料、鼓勵參加之後的標案」，是落選通知信常見的順序。「簽約後就開工」和沒有得標矛盾；公園處要僱園丁和信件主旨無關；「委員會下週會再開會審標」和前面說已經決定得標廠商矛盾。
下一批合約「涵蓋」除雪和街道清潔：contracts, which cover snow removal and street cleaning。retain（保留）、pursue（追求）、prevent（防止）放進去都不通，尤其 prevent snow removal 會變成「阻止除雪」。

p6.title: 電子郵件：年度績效面談
p6.text:
To: Daniel Ferreira
From: Ingrid Solberg
Date: June 1
Subject: Annual performance review

Hi Daniel,

It is time once again for annual performance reviews. Before we meet, please complete the self-assessment form that HR ___[1]___ to all employees last week. In it, you will be asked to describe your main accomplishments over the past year and to identify areas where you would like to grow.

I have tentatively scheduled your review for Thursday, June 11, at 2:00 P.M. If that time is inconvenient, let me know, and I will find another slot that works for ___[2]___. ___[3]___

Please bring any documents that you think support your self-assessment, such as client feedback or project reports. I look forward to a ___[4]___ conversation about your goals for the coming year.

Best,
Ingrid

blanks.exp: 句尾有 last week（上週），表示過去已完成的動作，用過去式 sent。sends 是現在式；will send 是未來式，和「上週」矛盾；has been sending 是現在完成進行式，表示一直持續在寄，不能和 last week 這種明確的過去時間連用。
找一個對「我們兩個人」都方便的時段：works for both of us。each other 和 one another 是「互相」，要用在雙方互相對彼此做某事的句子（例如 help each other），這裡沒有互相的動作；ourselves 是反身代名詞，主詞要是 we 才能用，這裡的主詞是 another slot。

opts: Please return your form to me before we meet.
Since your review was so positive, we will not need to meet.
HR has decided to discontinue annual reviews this year.
Client feedback surveys will be sent out in September.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：這段在安排面談時間，接著請對方「面談前把表格交給我」，連結了第一段的自評表和這段的面談日期，最連貫。「評價很好所以不用見面」和前面已經排好面談矛盾；「人資今年取消年度考核」和整封信的目的矛盾；九月寄客戶問卷和這次面談的安排無關。
期待一場「有成果的」對話：a productive conversation，是商務信件常見的結尾。punctual（準時的）用來形容人，不形容對話；tentative（暫定的）可以形容時間安排，不適合形容期待中的對話；mandatory（強制的）放在「我很期待」的句子裡語氣矛盾。

p6.title: 公告：自來水管線工程停水
p6.text:
NOTICE OF WATER SERVICE INTERRUPTION

The Calloway Water Authority will be replacing aging pipes along Birch Street between 3rd and 7th Avenues. ___[1]___, water service to homes and businesses on these blocks will be shut off on Tuesday, July 21, from 9:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M.

Residents are advised to store enough drinking water for the day ___[2]___ the work begins. When service is restored, tap water may appear cloudy for a short time. This is caused by air in the pipes and is not harmful. ___[3]___

We apologize for the inconvenience and thank residents for their patience as we work to improve the ___[4]___ of the local water supply.

blanks.exp: 因為要更換舊水管（原因），所以這幾個街區會停水（結果），用 As a result（因此）。In contrast（相對地）需要對比；Even so（即便如此）表示讓步，會變成「雖然換水管，還是停水」；For instance（例如）後面要舉例，停水不是換水管的例子。
居民應該在施工「開始之前」先儲水：before the work begins。since 表示「自從」或「因為」，「自從施工開始就儲水」不合理；unless（除非）、whereas（然而）的邏輯都不通。

opts: Running the tap briefly should clear it.
To be safe, please boil all tap water for the next two weeks.
Work on Birch Street was completed ahead of schedule last month.
Bills for July will be mailed a week later than usual.
blanks.exp: 句子插入題：前兩句說恢復供水後水可能混濁、但無害，接著提供解決方法「讓水龍頭流一下就會變清」，it 指混濁的自來水，最連貫。「為了安全請煮沸兩週」和前一句「無害」矛盾；「施工上個月已提前完成」和這份停水預告矛盾；帳單延後寄送和停水說明無關。
更換老舊水管是為了提升供水的「穩定可靠程度」：improve the reliability of the water supply。reliance（依賴）、relief（緩解、救濟）、relevance（關聯性）拼法相近，但放進去意思都不通。

p7.title: 單篇：會議室預約新規定
passages:

qs.q: What is the purpose of the notice?

p7.title: 單篇：文章（二手辦公家具）
passages:
Second Life for Office Furniture

By Renata Coleman

When companies relocate or downsize, their old desks and chairs often end up in landfills. Carlisle-based ReDesk is trying to change that. Founded four years ago by former interior designer Simone Achebe, the company collects used office furniture, repairs it, and resells it to businesses at about half the cost of new items. [1]

The idea came to Ms. Achebe while she was working on the redesign of a large law office. "The client was throwing away more than 200 chairs that were in perfectly good condition," she recalled. "Nobody had a plan for them." [2]

ReDesk now operates a 6,000-square-meter warehouse and employs 35 people, many of them skilled carpenters and upholsterers. Last year, the company kept an estimated 900 tons of furniture out of landfills. [3] Its clients range from small start-ups to a national bank, which recently furnished three regional offices entirely with ReDesk products.

Ms. Achebe admits that the business has faced obstacles. Supply is unpredictable, since it depends on when other firms decide to move, and some customers still assume that used furniture means lower quality. To address that concern, ReDesk now offers a five-year warranty on every item it sells. [4] "Once people see the furniture in person, they usually change their minds," she said.

qs.q: What is the article mainly about?
opts: A business that restores and resells used furniture
A law firm that moved into a new office
A new method of manufacturing desks
qs.exp: 第一段說 ReDesk collects used office furniture, repairs it, and resells it，後面各段介紹這家公司的起源、規模和挑戰＝一家整修並轉售二手家具的公司。律師事務所只是創辦人想到點子的場合；ReDesk 是修理舊家具，不是新的製造方法；文章沒有談家具漲價。

qs.q: The word "address" in paragraph 4, line 3, is closest in meaning to
qs.exp: To address that concern, ReDesk now offers a five-year warranty：為了「處理」顧客擔心品質的疑慮，提供五年保固，所以 address＝deal with。send（寄送，address a letter）、label（標上地址）、lecture（對…演說，address an audience）都是 address 在其他情境的意思，和 concern 搭配不通。

qs.q:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong?
"That moment convinced her to start a business of her own."
qs.exp: 這句的 That moment（那個時刻）需要前面先描述一個具體的時刻。[2] 前面正好是她在律師事務所看到兩百多張好椅子被丟掉、Nobody had a plan for them 的經歷，接著說這個時刻讓她決定創業，最連貫。[1] 前面講公司的營運方式、[3] 前面講去年的回收噸數、[4] 前面講保固，都沒有可以讓 That moment 指涉的事件。

qs.q: According to the article, why does ReDesk offer a warranty?
opts: To compete with a national bank
qs.exp: 依據 some customers still assume that used furniture means lower quality. To address that concern, ReDesk now offers a five-year warranty：保固是為了消除顧客對品質的疑慮。文中沒有提到法規要求；全國性銀行是 ReDesk 的客戶，不是競爭對手；技術工人是公司的員工，和保固無關。

p7.title: 單篇：服務中斷致歉電子郵件
passages:
To: Benedikt Hoffmann <bhoffmann@hoffmannbakeries.com>
From: Yuki Nakamura <ynakamura@stratuscloud.com>
Date: November 5
Subject: Service disruption on November 3

Dear Mr. Hoffmann,

Thank you for your message regarding the outage that affected your online ordering system on Tuesday, November 3. I understand that your customers were unable to place orders for nearly four hours during your busiest morning period, and I sincerely apologize. [1]

Our engineers have identified the cause. A routine software update was installed on one of our servers without being properly tested, and it caused a conflict with several client applications, including yours. [2] We have since introduced an additional review step so that no update can be installed until it has been tested on a separate system.

In recognition of the disruption, we will credit your account with the equivalent of one full month of service. This credit will appear automatically on your December invoice. [3]

I would also like to offer you a free consultation with one of our technical specialists, who can review your current setup and recommend ways to make it more resilient. [4] Please let me know a few dates that would suit you.

Sincerely,
Yuki Nakamura
Client Relations Manager, Stratus Cloud Services

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the e-mail?
opts: To announce a planned software update
To request payment of an overdue invoice
To introduce a new online ordering system
qs.exp: 開頭 Thank you for your message regarding the outage … I sincerely apologize，可知 Hoffmann 先生先來信反映服務中斷，這封是回覆並道歉＝回應客訴。軟體更新是造成中斷的原因，不是預告；信中是給對方帳戶補償（credit），不是催繳；線上訂購系統是 Hoffmann 先生原本就在用的，不是新系統。

qs.q: What has Stratus Cloud Services changed?
opts: The price of its monthly service
The servers it uses for bakeries
qs.exp: 依據 We have since introduced an additional review step so that no update can be installed until it has been tested on a separate system：新增審查步驟，更新要先在另一個系統測試才能安裝＝改變安裝更新的程序。一個月的補償是一次性的，沒有調整月費；沒有提到換伺服器或客服時間。

qs.q: The word "resilient" in paragraph 4, line 2, is closest in meaning to
qs.exp: recommend ways to make it more resilient：在這次中斷事件的脈絡下，是讓系統設定「更耐得住問題、更可靠」，resilient＝dependable。temporary（暫時的）和「更耐得住問題」相反；affordable（便宜的）、attractive（吸引人的）都和防止中斷無關。

qs.q:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong?
"No further action is required on your part."
qs.exp: [3] 前面說補償金額 will appear automatically on your December invoice（自動出現在帳單上），接著說「您不需要做任何事」最連貫。[4] 前面是提供免費諮詢，後面還請對方提供方便的日期，說「不需要做任何事」會矛盾；[1] 前面是道歉、[2] 前面是說明原因，都沒有需要對方採取行動的事項。

p7.title: 單篇：報導（老戲院變共享廚房）

Old Theater Finds New Purpose as Shared Kitchen

BRAMLEY (February 24) — The Rialto, a 1920s movie theater on Bramley's Main Street that had stood empty since 2019, will reopen next month as a shared commercial kitchen for small food businesses. [1]

The project is the work of Bramley Food Hub, a nonprofit organization that helps local cooks turn their recipes into businesses. Members will be able to rent fully equipped kitchen space by the hour, which spares them the expense of building their own facilities. [2] Rates will start at $18 an hour, with reduced rates for overnight bookings.

Renovation costs of $1.2 million were covered by a state grant and donations from more than 300 residents. The building's original facade and ticket booth have been preserved, and the former lobby will serve as a small café where members can sell their products to the public. [3]

According to director Farah Haddad, 27 businesses have already signed up, including bakers, caterers, and a company that produces hot sauce. "Many of our members currently cook in their own homes, which limits how much they can sell," Ms. Haddad said. "Here, they will have room to grow." [4] The hub will hold an open house on Saturday, March 14, from 10 A.M. to 3 P.M.

qs.q: What is NOT mentioned about the Rialto building?
opts: It will continue to show films on weekends
Parts of its original design were kept
It has been unused for several years
Its renovation was partly funded by residents
qs.exp: 文章說戲院將改成共享廚房，沒有說週末還會放電影＝不符。保留原始設計：original facade and ticket booth have been preserved；閒置多年：had stood empty since 2019；居民出資：donations from more than 300 residents。

qs.q: The word "spares" in paragraph 2, line 3, is closest in meaning to
qs.exp: which spares them the expense of building their own facilities：按時數租廚房「讓他們省下」自己蓋廚房的費用，spare someone something＝save someone something。lends（借出）不通；keeps in reserve（留作備用）是 spare 當形容詞「備用的」的意思；forgives（原諒、免除債務）語意不對。

qs.q:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong?
"The theater's old projectors, however, have been donated to a film museum."
qs.exp: 這句用 however 表示對比：[3] 前面說戲院的外牆和售票亭都被「保留」下來，接著說「不過舊放映機已捐給電影博物館」，保留和移走形成對比，最連貫。[1] 前面只說戲院要改成廚房，沒有「保留」可以對比；[2] 前面講會員租用廚房、[4] 前面講會員的成長空間，和放映機都接不上。

qs.q: What is suggested about many Food Hub members?
opts: They used to work at the Rialto theater
They plan to open restaurants on Main Street
They will be able to cook overnight for free
qs.exp: 依據 Many of our members currently cook in their own homes, which limits how much they can sell：在家裡做菜限制了銷售量。文中沒有說他們以前在戲院工作或要在 Main Street 開餐廳；夜間租用是 reduced rates（降價），不是免費。

Lena Park [11:10 A.M.]

Owen Kessler [11:11 A.M.]

She is offering to support Mr. Kessler

p7.title: 訊息：更換研習講師
passages:
